It permits copying and distributing the document's contents, or portions of them, in any medium for any purpose, provided every copy carries a link to the original, the pre-existing copyright notice, and the document's status; it grants NO right to modify. So this entry holds the text verbatim and changes no wording: the link, notice and status are on its first two page sections (page-001, page-002) and repeated in `note`. Splitting it into per-page files is a reading of 'portions' and of 'any medium', recorded here so the owner can overrule it, as for w3c-2013-prov-o (issue #1614).
note: Source: uploads/w3c-2024-prov-jsonld-submission.pdf (sha256 ab826cd4a4cfe750c6b7eac6a8439b21c1114af747e3a1a05f48de7b4472c230, 71 pages), a browser print (Chrome 154 / Skia PDF, created 2026-10-01) of the HTML specification; every page carries the print's running header and footer ('10/1/26, 6:17 PM', 'The PROV-JSONLD Serialization', 'https://www.w3.org/submissions/prov-jsonld/', 'N/71'), which are NOT stripped because the page rung has no such option. The printed URL is the latest-version URL; the document's own header identifies the text as 'W3C Member Submission 25 August 2024', 'This version: https://www.w3.org/submissions/2024/SUBM-prov-jsonld-20240825/', 'Latest published version: https://www.w3.org/submissions/prov-jsonld/', editors Luc Moreau and Dong Huynh (King's College London). In this print each heading's '§' self-link text is extracted at the END of the page the heading is on, not at the heading's position.
